name: Lanyard
description: A feedback board’s public roadmap: three bordered lane panels with a coloured dot in each head, a square vote box on the left of every card, an uppercase theme eyebrow, and an item page with its voters in a left-hand rail.
features: Preset: board — three lane panels (Under review / Planned / In progress) with a tinted dot and a hairline under each head
Square vote box with a chevron at the start of each card; uppercase theme eyebrow; no excerpt
Sort row (Trending / Top / New), tags and search above the board
Item page: the voters, vote and Follow in a rail on the left; the team’s answer under the title
Zero custom CSS — every detail is a theme setting

sections.problem: We plan launches across several teams and cannot see how the pieces line up in time.
sections.proposal: A timeline view of items with start and due dates, dependencies drawn as arrows, drag to reschedule.

comments.author: tomas
comments.markdown: Dependencies are the part we need most — the bars alone we can fake with a spreadsheet.

sections.problem: Weekly reviews and monthly invoicing are the same task every time. We recreate them by hand and sometimes forget.
sections.proposal: Repeat a task daily, weekly, monthly or on a custom rule. The next one is created when the current one is done.

comments.author: maya
comments.markdown: Please support "last working day of the month" — that is when our payroll runs.

sections.problem: Moving forty items to a new owner after a reorganisation means forty separate edits.
sections.proposal: Select several items and change their owner, status, labels or due date in one go.

comments.author: priya
comments.markdown: An undo for the bulk change would make people much less nervous to use it.

items.title: Single sign-on with Okta and Entra ID
items.author: devon

sections.problem: Our security policy requires every tool to sit behind our identity provider. Without SSO we cannot roll this out beyond a pilot team.
sections.proposal: SAML and OIDC sign-in, with just-in-time provisioning and the option to make SSO the only way in.

comments.author: maya
comments.markdown: SCIM deprovisioning would be the second half of this for us — removing leavers by hand is a risk.

comments.author: priya
comments.markdown: Same request from three of our larger customers this quarter.

response.author: team
response.markdown: This is planned for the autumn. We are starting with SAML and Okta, then Entra ID; SCIM follows in the same project.

sections.problem: Finance needs our numbers in a spreadsheet every month. Today someone copies tables by hand, and it is easy to miss a row.
sections.proposal: An Export button on every report that downloads exactly what is on screen, filters included.

response.author: team
response.markdown: Planned. Every report will get an Export button that respects the filters on screen.

sections.problem: When a setting changes, nobody can say who changed it or when. Our auditors ask for this every year.
sections.proposal: A searchable log of admin actions — who, what, when, from where — exportable for a date range.

comments.author: devon
comments.markdown: Retention of at least a year would cover our SOC 2 window.

response.author: team
response.markdown: Planned, with a year of retention on every paid plan.

items.title: Send alerts to a Slack channel
items.author: devon

sections.problem: Our team lives in Slack. Email alerts get buried, so we find out about a failed sync hours later.
sections.proposal: Pick a channel per workspace, choose which events post there, and link each message back to the item.

comments.author: devon
comments.markdown: Being able to pick events per channel would matter for us — #ops wants failures, #general does not.

response.author: team
response.markdown: We are building this now. Channels are chosen per workspace and each channel picks its own events.

sections.problem: Many of us work late or in dim rooms, and the bright white canvas is tiring after a few hours. The browser extensions that force a dark theme break the charts and the editor.
sections.proposal: A dark scheme that follows the system setting, with a manual switch in your profile. Charts and the editor get their own dark palette rather than an inverted one.

comments.author: ines
comments.markdown: Please make sure the chart colours are designed for dark, not just inverted. Inverted reds and greens are unreadable.

comments.author: team
comments.markdown: Agreed — the charts get their own palette. We are testing it with a few colour-blind users first.

response.author: team
response.markdown: In progress — the editor and navigation are done; charts are next.

sections.problem: Accounts protected by a password alone are the first thing our security review flags.
sections.proposal: Authenticator-app codes and passkeys, with recovery codes and an admin switch to require it.

response.author: team
response.markdown: In progress: authenticator apps first, passkeys right after.
